title: Build the position-wise feedforward network
statement:
Step 9 · Transformer block

The same feedforward weights transform every token independently. A first affine layer expands features, ReLU adds a nonlinearity, and a second layer projects back. Modern models may use other activations.

Build it

Compute ReLU(x @ w1 + b1) @ w2 + b2. Matrices have valid compatible shapes; weights use input-by-output orientation.

Contract: Implement feedforward using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: x = [1, -1], w1 = [[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, -1]], b1 = [0, 0, 0], w2 = [[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]], b2 = [0, 0]
Expected: [3, 2]
Input: x = [0, 0], w1 = [[1], [1]], b1 = [-2], w2 = [[3, 4]], b2 = [1, 2]
Expected: [1, 2]
Hint

The affine helper handles the matrix-vector arithmetic. Apply ReLU only between the two projections.

Review your understanding

What changes if you remove the nonlinearity?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
